_comment_streams: Keyed by streamLabel, an ORDERED list of stream attempts. The v4 streamMessage mock finds the call's `originalMessage` MARKER inside any user message (the oracle puts it in the primary/failover messages; the recovery service embeds it in its recovery user message too), resolves the label, then pops the next attempt in order — so a tool-unsupported retry / empty retry / the primary-then-recovery pair, all re-issuing streams, get DIFFERENT sequences. Each chunk: {content}, {reasoning} (cumulative), {done, usage?}, or {error}.

calls.comment: v4 65f5021c8: runPrimaryStream's catch-all now routes an auth failure through the chain. The named understudy answers and state.effectiveProfile swaps to it.

calls.name: hard_error_chain_exhausted
calls.originalMessage: every candidate is indisposed tonight
calls.comment: Understudy AND the tier pick both fail: the chain is exhausted, the buffers are left empty, and the rethrown error carries summarizeFallbackAttempts' roll.

calls.name: hard_error_routed_direct_dangerous
calls.originalMessage: an unmoderated turn headed straight for the uncensored desk
calls.comment: P4.D228 (v4 ce2f1dabf, #77): an Unmoderated turn writes NO per-message dangerFlags any more; `routedDirect` keeps the failover treating its content as dangerous. The orchestrator's contentTreatedAsDangerous reaches this seam as isDangerousRouted: true with no flag anywhere -- the chain then clears the tier picks, the same script as hard_error_chain_exhausted run dangerous.

calls.name: hard_error_after_content
calls.originalMessage: the curtain falls mid-line
calls.comment: Content already reached the user, so the chain is SKIPPED and the partial is preserved as before. restreamInto appends and SSE has no reset.

calls.name: hard_error_not_eligible
calls.originalMessage: a prompt too long for anyone
calls.comment: classifyFallbackTrigger refuses a token limit, so the chain never runs and the request-limit recovery keeps its exclusive claim.

calls.name: empty_chain_fallback
calls.originalMessage: an empty house three times over
calls.comment: The THIRD recovery: same-provider retry empty, off duty, so the chain walks and the understudy answers.

calls.name: hard_error_resets_dirty_buffers
calls.originalMessage: the primary thinks aloud and then collapses
calls.comment: P4.D135: the primary emits REASONING and then dies. hasStartedStreaming stays false (only content sets it), so the chain runs — and the understudy's answer must not be glued onto the corpse of the one before it. resetStreamingBuffersForSwap is what makes that true, and only a DIRTY-buffer case can tell it from a no-op: the buffers are compared.

calls.name: hard_error_vision_skips_understudy
calls.originalMessage: the turn is carrying a picture
calls.comment: P4.D136 (v4 a1d88aa3a, bug 106): `needsVision` is now read from what the message ARRAY carries, not from what the user uploaded. `attachedFiles` is EMPTY here and the array carries an image — the pre-fix spelling reads the uploads and calls the turn text-only, so the OPENAI understudy (no supportsImageUpload) answers. Post-fix the chain filters it out, the tier pick is filtered too, and the exhausted chain rethrows with summarizeFallbackAttempts' roll. The two spellings disagree on this one case and agree on every other.

calls.name: empty_walk_exhausts_on_empty
calls.originalMessage: every understudy is as silent as the house
calls.comment: P4.68 — the chain walk EXHAUSTING from the empty-response path. Measured before adding it: every `chainAttempts` entry in this corpus carried trigger `empty-response` and no walk ever recorded all THREE candidates; `empty_chain_fallback` stops at two because the tier spare answers. This row drives v4 provider-failover.service.ts:637 for the last candidate too, and pins the exhausted outcome (empty `fullResponse`, effectiveProfile left on the primary).

calls.name: empty_walk_understudy_errors_then_tier_ok
calls.originalMessage: the understudy drops the tray and the spare recovers it
calls.comment: P4.68 — fail-then-recover INSIDE the walk, and the only `provider-error` chain trigger in the corpus. A candidate THROWS (provider-failover.service.ts:622 records it under its trigger) and the walk continues to one that succeeds. Everything else here either goes empty the whole way down or fails the whole way down; nothing covered a throw followed by a recovery, so `recordAttempt`'s error branch and the post-error effectiveProfile swap were both unmeasured.

calls.name: empty_walk_auth_refusals
calls.originalMessage: every understudy refuses at the door
calls.comment: P4.74 — the credential-gate chain arm (v4 provider-failover.service.ts:583-591), the third blind spot P4.68 measured and deferred. Runs on its OWN primary (`profileKey`) so no existing case's tier pool moves: both candidates it offers are refused before a stream is ever opened, recording trigger `auth` with v4's two reason spellings — `no-api-key-configured` from the CONFIGURED understudy and `api-key-not-found` from the TIER PICK, whose dangling apiKeyId passes the picker's static credential check and only fails at the gate.

calls.name: empty_retry_throws_then_chain
calls.originalMessage: the retry itself falls over
calls.comment: P4.D173: the retry arm that THREW. v4 records a `retry`/`failed` row from the thrown error's message (trigger from classifyFallbackTrigger, else provider-error) and logs '[EmptyResponse] Same-provider retry failed'; the port had discarded the error with `let _ = restream_into(...)`. The chain then walks and the understudy answers, so the trail reads opener → retry → understudy-answered.

calls.name: empty_reroute_throws_then_chain
calls.originalMessage: the uncensored desk falls over
calls.comment: P4.D173: the uncensored reroute arm that THREW. Flagged content skips the same-profile retry, so the opener is recorded with the INFERRED moderation verdict; the reroute's own call falls over and is recorded against `route.connection_profile` (the swap only happens on success, so nothing else would name it); the chain then answers.

calls.name: hard_error_stall_before_first_chunk
calls.originalMessage: the provider takes the request and says nothing at all
calls.comment: P4.D189 (v4 f90144ac4, bug 141): the primary answers with headers and then goes quiet before its first chunk. classifyFallbackTrigger reads LLMStreamStalledError by NAME as `network` — its message matches no network pattern — so the chain runs and the understudy answers. Without the named arm this records `provider-error`.

calls.name: hard_error_stall_mid_stream
calls.originalMessage: two lines land and then the wire goes dead
calls.comment: P4.D189: the stall arrives AFTER content reached the user, so `hasStartedStreaming` skips the chain exactly as it does for any other mid-stream hard error (restreamInto appends and SSE has no reset). The turn's error is the stall itself and the partial is preserved. The `content_then_error` sibling is the same shape with an ordinary provider error.

calls.name: empty_walk_understudy_stalls_then_tier_ok
calls.originalMessage: the understudy goes quiet and the spare recovers it
calls.comment: P4.D189: a stall INSIDE the walk. The understudy leg records `network` — not the `provider-error` its sibling empty_walk_understudy_errors_then_tier_ok records — and the walk continues to the tier spare.

calls.name: empty_retry_stalls_then_chain
calls.originalMessage: the same-provider retry goes quiet
calls.comment: P4.D189: the empty-response same-provider retry STALLS. The trail records retry/failed with the stalled message as its detail and `network` as its trigger; the chain then walks and the understudy answers. Its sibling empty_retry_throws_then_chain uses a network-PATTERNED message, so the trigger alone would not discriminate — this one's message matches nothing, and only the named arm makes it `network`.

calls.name: empty_reroute_stalls_then_chain
calls.originalMessage: the uncensored desk goes quiet
calls.comment: P4.D189: the Concierge reroute STALLS. Flagged content skips the same-profile retry, so the opener carries the inferred moderation verdict; the reroute is recorded against route.connection_profile with `network`, and the chain then answers.

calls.name: tool_unsupported_retry_success_bare
calls.originalMessage: kindly summon a bare helper
calls.comment: P4.97: the retry's clears proven against a BARE primary too — no previousResponseId, no stop. The cache key is still set (runPrimaryStream passes `characterId` unconditionally, so the funnel always derives one), which is what makes this the one-key twin of tool_unsupported_retry_success rather than a no-key case. Appended LAST: the option-bag side-channel is an ORDERED per-call list, so a case inserted mid-array would shift every following index. Its marker deliberately shares no substring with any other: the mock resolves a label by FIRST containing marker, so `please invoke a helper, bare` would have resolved to tool_unsupported_then_ok and died on an exhausted cursor (measured).

calls.name: inform_consumed_by_preserved_partial
calls.originalMessage: a passage for the lamplighter
calls.comment: P4.106 item 2 — v4 `primary-stream.service.test.ts:227`: a preserved partial IS a persisted assistant turn and the model read the inform, so the turn's rows are consumed against the PRESERVED (pre-generated) message id. Rows planted through v4's REAL repository (the top-level `informs`); a third row for the same seat is NOT in this turn's informRowIds and must stay pending. Appended LAST (the ordered option-bag rule above).

calls.name: inform_untouched_when_turn_carried_none
calls.originalMessage: no passage for the gardener
calls.comment: P4.106 item 2 — v4 `primary-stream.service.test.ts:249`: a turn that carried no inform touches nothing, even though the seat HAS a pending row (planted) — the preserve consumes only what the turn's context carried.

calls.name: empty_auto_route_scan_without_configured_id
calls.originalMessage: no configured desk, but the scan finds one
calls.comment: P4.D225 (v4 8bd080267, #73): the empty-body reroute's gate dropped its `uncensoredTextProfileId` conjunct. On duty with NO desk text id (P4.D227: the retired Auto-Route) still asks the understudy resolver (whose scan is the answer); pre-#73 this case skipped the reroute and walked the chain.

calls.name: empty_flagged_nobody_to_ask
calls.originalMessage: flagged, and nobody uncensored to ask
calls.comment: P4.D225: flagged content opens with the INFERRED refusal (refusalWasStated counts it), the resolver answers nobody, so the Concierge posts `refusal-no-understudy` (purpose text) and the chain walks. An inferred refusal is NOT recordable: the ledger stays at zero.

calls.name: empty_retry_states_refusal_rerouted
calls.originalMessage: the retry names content_filter and the desk answers
calls.comment: P4.D225: the opening is a plain empty body; the same-provider retry comes back empty with a STATED finish reason (content_filter), which becomes the turn's refusal. The understudy answers, so the ledger records it with rerouted=true (one per turn, on the way out).

calls.name: hard_refusal_understudy_answers
calls.originalMessage: a thrown refusal the desk answers
calls.comment: P4.D225: a thrown TYPED refusal (the plugin contract's real ModerationRejectionError) classifies as moderation-refusal with evidence typed-error. On duty (P4.D227: the retired Auto-Route) the understudy is tried FIRST (substitute: true) and answers: recovered, trail refused -> answered via concierge, ledger +1 rerouted=true, no chain walk.

calls.name: hard_refusal_understudy_refuses_then_chain
calls.originalMessage: the desk refuses as well
calls.comment: P4.D225: the understudy's own call throws a refusal too, recorded refused/moderation-refusal against the understudy (not failed). Ledger +1 rerouted=false, then the refusing profile's chain walks with dangerous: true and the understudy in alreadyTried. The named understudy then falls over (503), so whether the TIER PICK is offered is what shows the `dangerous: true` override: a pick must be cleared for the content.

calls.name: hard_refusal_off_duty_not_permitted
calls.originalMessage: the mode forbids the reroute
calls.comment: P4.D225: a thrown refusal the Concierge may not reroute (P4.D227, v4 `3b463d6b1` #76: off duty — the retired DETECT_ONLY had no successor): the INFO line with the policy's source/state, the ledger (rerouted=false), and the chain with the context's own dangerous flag. No understudy lookup at all.

calls.name: hard_refusal_no_understudy
calls.originalMessage: auto-route but no uncensored desk anywhere
calls.comment: P4.D225: on duty, but the resolver answers nobody: WARN, the `refusal-no-understudy` bubble (a thrown refusal is always stated), the ledger, then the chain cleared for the content.

calls.name: hard_refusal_without_settings
calls.originalMessage: a refusal with no Concierge settings handed in
calls.comment: P4.D225: `conciergePolicy` absent (v4's optional; `dangerSettings` before P4.D227): the not-permitted INFO with the source/state undefined, the ledger, the chain.

calls.name: empty_locked_mid_turn_not_rerouted
calls.originalMessage: the operator locks it while the provider thinks
calls.comment: P4.D226 (v4 `4d370a90f`, `reads the state at refusal time: a chat locked while the provider was thinking is not rerouted`): the turn began Moderated (no snapshot), the row is Locked; the same-provider retry STATES content_filter, the refusal-time re-read says Locked — the INFO line, `refusal-not-permitted` (reason locked), NO uncensored retry, the ledger records rerouted=false, and the chain walks.

calls.name: empty_plain_empty_on_a_locked_chat
calls.originalMessage: a plain empty body on a Locked chat
calls.comment: P4.D226 (v4 `posts nothing for a plain empty body on a Locked chat`): no stated refusal anywhere, so no announcement; Locked still bars the uncensored retry; the chain walks.

calls.name: hard_refusal_on_a_locked_chat
calls.originalMessage: a thrown refusal on a Locked chat
calls.comment: P4.D226 (v4 `never asks the uncensored understudy, and says the refusal stands`): on duty, a thrown TYPED refusal, the chat Locked — the INFO line, `refusal-not-permitted` (reason locked), the ledger rerouted=false, no understudy lookup, and the chain walks with the context's own dangerous flag.

calls.name: hard_refusal_locked_mid_turn
calls.originalMessage: a thrown refusal on a chat locked mid-turn
calls.comment: P4.D226 (v4 `reads the state at refusal time: a chat locked mid-turn is not rerouted`): the turn's chat reads Moderated, the row is Locked — the re-read's INFO (state changed), then the Locked arm.

calls.name: empty_sent_off_duty_mid_turn_not_rerouted
calls.originalMessage: an empty turn after the operator sent him off duty
calls.comment: P4.D227 (v4 `3b463d6b1`, #76): the turn began on duty, but the operator sends the Concierge off duty while the provider thinks; `readCurrentConciergeOnDuty` is re-asked at refusal time (the on-duty INFO), so the stated refusal is not rerouted.

calls.name: hard_refusal_sent_off_duty_mid_call
calls.originalMessage: a thrown refusal once he was off duty
calls.comment: P4.D227 (v4 `3b463d6b1`, #76): the thrown refusal on a turn that began on duty, after the Concierge went off duty mid-call: the refusal-time re-read says no, the not-permitted INFO carries the policy source/state, the chain runs.

calls.name: hard_sdk_code_understudy_answers
calls.originalMessage: a coded 400 the desk answers
calls.comment: P4.118: an openai-SDK 400 whose ONLY moderation evidence is its code (Azure's content_filter under benign wording, which matches no message pattern). v4's APIError carries code + error.code, so classifyFallbackTrigger answers moderation-refusal with evidence provider-code; on duty the uncensored desk is tried first and answers. v5 reaches the same only through the refusal SIDE its transport error now carries (model::provider_error). Before P4.118 v5's HTTP 400 message fell to the 4xx rule: not fallback-eligible.

calls.name: hard_sdk_uncoded_not_eligible
calls.originalMessage: an uncoded 400 nobody reroutes
calls.comment: P4.118: the twin with code null. No evidence at all (the wording matches no pattern), so the 4xx rule answers null on both sides: not fallback-eligible, no reroute, no trail, the error rethrown. The thrown message differs by the order's §S.5 bytes (v4 '400 …', v5 'HTTP 400: …'), pinned both ways in the harness.

calls.name: hard_stream_frame_code_rerouted
calls.originalMessage: a coded frame before any content
calls.comment: P4.122: the stream opens 200 and its FIRST frame is `data: {"error":{...,"code":"content_filter"}}`; openai 7.23.0's Stream.fromSSEResponse throws new APIError(undefined, data.error) - no status, message = error.message, code + error.code = content_filter. hasStartedStreaming is still false, so v4's attemptHardErrorFailover classifies moderation-refusal with evidence provider-code and the uncensored desk answers. v5 reaches the same only through the decoder's refusal side (DecodeError -> decode_stream_error); before P4.122 v5's decoder dropped the frame and the turn took the EMPTY-response path.

calls.name: hard_stream_frame_after_content_kept
calls.originalMessage: a coded frame after content
calls.comment: P4.122: the twin AFTER one content chunk. hasStartedStreaming flipped on the content, so neither side fails over; the partial is kept by preservePartialOnError and the error rethrown.

calls.name: hard_stream_frame_uncoded
calls.originalMessage: an uncoded frame before any content
calls.comment: P4.122: an uncoded frame `{"error":{"message":...}}` - a status-less, code-less APIError whose message matches no pattern. Whatever v4's classifyFallbackTrigger answers is the measurement both sides pin.
